intent.objective: Bound the memory the tree materialiser uses: materialize_tree in tools/agentctl/agentctl/check_environment.py must refuse, with the module's existing CandidateTreeUnsafe error, a tree in which any single blob exceeds 32 MiB or whose blobs total more than 256 MiB, and must leave no partial tree behind
intent.rationale: materialize_tree reads each blob fully into memory (process.stdout.read(int(header[2]))) with no size bound while building check trees, so a candidate that commits one huge blob can exhaust control-plane memory before any sandbox limit applies (independent review B3 finding 5).
non_goals: Changing the sandbox, its limits, or run_candidate_checks semantics
Changing the safety rules the materialiser already enforces (forbidden path components, duplicate or clashing entries, O_NOFOLLOW, symlink handling)
Modifying any existing test or any file other than the two writable files
acceptance_behavior: A named module-level constant limits one blob to 32 MiB (32 * 1024 * 1024 bytes) and another limits the total of all blob sizes to 256 MiB (256 * 1024 * 1024 bytes); both are in the module's __all__ or documented in the materialize_tree docstring

A tree containing a single blob larger than the per-blob limit makes materialize_tree raise CandidateTreeUnsafe, before the oversized blob's content is read into memory (the size is taken from the cat-file header or a size listing, and the blob is not read)
A tree whose blobs are each within the per-blob limit but total more than the total limit makes materialize_tree raise CandidateTreeUnsafe
After either refusal the destination directory does not exist (no partial tree left behind), also when the refusal was detected after some entries were already written

A blob of exactly the per-blob limit and a tree totalling exactly the total limit are accepted; ordinary trees (small files, executable files, symlinks, nested directories) materialise byte for byte exactly as before
The error message names the offending path (per-blob case) or states the total limit (total case)

scope.expected_change_shape: Two module constants, a pre-read size check in materialize_tree with cleanup of the destination on refusal, and one new test module

deterministic_checks: PYTHONPATH=tools/agentctl python3 -m unittest discover -s tools/agentctl/tests -t tools/agentctl -p test_materialise_limits.py
PYTHONPATH=tools/agentctl python3 -m unittest discover -s tools/agentctl/tests -t tools/agentctl -p test_plan_loading.py
PYTHONPATH=tools/agentctl python3 -m unittest discover -s tools/agentctl/tests -t tools/agentctl -p test_context_staleness.py
behavioral_requirements: The new tests build real Git repositories in temporary directories (git init, git add, git commit through subprocess, with a fixed local identity configured per repository) and call materialize_tree directly with an ObjectReader on that repository; they must NOT call run_candidate_checks, sandbox.probe or runc, because the tests themselves run inside the runc sandbox where runc does not exist

To keep the tests fast and the disk use small, the tests may patch the module constants (for example with unittest.mock.patch.object on the module) to small values; at least one test must instead use the real constants with a blob of exactly 32 MiB plus 1 byte (accepted vs refused boundary) written sparsely or as zero bytes, and one with exactly 32 MiB, so the real limit value is protected; do not create more than about 70 MiB of test data in total
A regression test shows the pre-change failure: an oversized blob is materialised without error on the unchanged code (the tests fail on the original source and pass after the change)

The tests cover: per-blob refusal, total refusal, exact-limit acceptance, destination absent after refusal (including a refusal detected after earlier small files were already written), the unchanged byte-for-byte result for an ordinary tree with an executable file and a symlink, and that the refusal is CandidateTreeUnsafe (assertRaises) and not another exception

Every test in the new module passes inside the check environment: uid 65534, no network, no runc, a private synthetic Git repository at /work with a single commit, HOME=/tmp, only /tmp and /work writable; use tempfile under /tmp and locate the repository root with pathlib from __file__, never with git rev-parse of the working directory
definition_of_done: The candidate passes the deterministic checks, receives an independent review with no blocking findings, and is integrated unchanged

replan_conditions: The fix needs a file outside the writable set
